title: Prospect Playbook - Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pitch Deck & Security FAQ
author: Avery Chen
content:
Summary:
This playbook gives AE/SDR/SE teams a single-page reference for positioning Redwood Inference to engineering and platform buyers at prospect-stage meetings. It combines concise positioning and messaging, competitive brief talking points, an annotated pitch-deck outline, pricing guidance for early sizing conversations, two short case studies for social proof, a prospect-facing security FAQ, and a recommended demo/discovery script.

1) One-line positioning
Redwood Inference: a production-first inference platform that makes LLM serving predictable, cost-effective, and portable across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

2) Elevator pitches (30s / 1 min / 3 min)
- 30s: "Redwood helps engineering teams ship LLM features with production-grade latency, cost controls, and deployment flexibility — whether you want a hosted API, reserved GPU capacity, or a private VPC/on-prem install."
- 1m: "We combine a GPU-optimized serving runtime, model and quantization guidance, and unified operational tooling (observability, rollouts, tracing) so teams get predictable latency and unit economics without building their own serving stack."
- 3m: Quick problem -> value mapping: "Customers come to us when AWS/GCP endpoints are unpredictable or their self-hosted stack becomes expensive to operate. Redwood reduces per-token cost with batching/caching and intelligent routing, guarantees capacity via Dedicated, and supports strict security needs via Private deployments — all while giving engineers the same API and observability."

3) Messaging pillars (use by persona)
- Engineering / ML Infra:
  - Production-first runtime: latency SLOs, continuous batching, KV cache, and attention/kernels tuned for inference workloads.
  - Predictable capacity: Dedicated GPU pools + autoscaling policies.
  - Easy dev experience: same REST/SDK and model catalog for hosted and private modes.
- Product / Growth:
  - Fast time-to-value: hosted API + quickstart templates and SDKs for product experiments.
  - Cost controls: token-level billing, automated batching/cache suggestions, and quantization profiles.
- Security / Compliance:
  - Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) with KMS/HSM support, audit logs, and role-based controls.
  - SOC/ISO readiness (see security FAQ).

4) Competitive brief - quick talking points
- Against general cloud AI endpoints (managed endpoints from hyperscalers):
  - Win: Clearer unit economics and production tooling for inference (batching/cache/quantization) and predictable Dedicated capacity.
  - Lose: Hyperscalers may have deeper integrations with other cloud services — we frame this as "best-of-breed inference with multi-cloud portability."
- Against LLM API providers (convenience-first):
  - Win: Lower unit cost at scale, enterprise SLAs, Dedicated/Private for isolation and compliance.
  - Lose: Some convenience platforms have larger model catalogs; we emphasize curated open models + Redwood-verified performance.
- Against self-hosted inference stacks:
  - Win: Faster time-to-production, support and observability, and lower operational overhead.
  - Lose: In highly optimized, extremely large internal teams the capex model can appear cheaper — counter with TCO examples.

5) Objection handling (short)
- "We can host ourselves": Ask about ongoing ops cost, headcount, and SLOs. Offer TCO example and invite them to benchmark with our eval-harness.
- "Security/compliance concerns": Point to Private deployment, KMS/HSM, audit logging and our SOC/ISO posture. Offer to run architecture review with solutions engineering.
- "Pricing transparency": Walk through token-level billing, cost reports in Console, and Optimize recommendations that show expected savings from batching/quantization.

6) Annotated pitch deck (slides + speaking notes)
- Slide 1: Title / TL;DR - Problem we solve (latency, cost, reliability) and one-liner.
- Slide 2: Market & Momentum - growth of LLM usage and shifts from model ownership to serving.
- Slide 3: Product overview - Hosted API, Dedicated, Private, Console, Optimize.
- Slide 4: Architecture highlights - serving runtime, smart routing, batching & KV cache (1 diagram).
- Slide 5: Key differentiators - production-first, unified runtime across environments, cost controls.
- Slide 6: Enterprise features - SLAs, Private deployment, audit logs, RBAC, KMS.
- Slide 7: Pricing & procurement - simple example pricing for hosted and Dedicated (see section 8).
- Slide 8: Case studies - two short examples (on next section).
- Slide 9: Security & compliance - summary and offer to share evidence package.
- Slide 10: Next steps / pilot offer - quick start credits, POC checklist, owner contacts.

Speaking notes: keep slides < 10 mins for initial discovery demo; use live Console to show latency/cost breakdown and a short inferencing demo (3-4 prompts) configured for the prospect's expected sequence length.

7) Pricing guidance (initial framework for AE sizing conversations)
- Hosted (self-serve):
  - Starter: best for experiments; per-token pricing with free credits.
  - Production: per-token with volume break tiers.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity):
  - Monthly commit for GPU pool (example): small (1-2 GPUs), medium (4-8), large (16+). Pricing depends on GPU class and reserved concurrency.
- Private: base platform licensing + deployment support and optional on-prem packaging.

Example conversation snippets (don't quote numbers publicly):
- "For a product with 100k monthly active users and average 200 tokens per call, our back-of-envelope shows Xk tokens/month which maps to Hosted cost Y; a Dedicated pool often becomes cost-effective above Z tokens/month."

8) Case studies (short)
- Case study A - Conversational commerce startup (Mid-market):
  - Problem: Intermittent latency and rising per-token cost on third-party endpoints.
  - Approach: Switched to Redwood Hosted with batching and prefix caching, then migrated high-volume flows to Dedicated.
  - Outcome: 40% reduction in per-token cost, 60ms median latency improvement on key routes, and predictable 99.9% availability with Dedicated.
- Case study B - Regulated finance customer (Enterprise):
  - Problem: Data residency and audit requirements prevented cloud-hosted third-party APIs.
  - Approach: Private deployment in customer VPC + HSM-managed keys and dedicated SLAs.
  - Outcome: Successful pilot in 8 weeks, passed internal audit for data-in-transit/at-rest controls, and enabled a 3x faster customer support triage flow using LLM summaries.

9) Security FAQ (for prospects)
- Q: Can we run Redwood in our VPC or on-prem?
  - A: Yes - Private deployments support VPC and on-prem packaging. We provide an architecture review, installation playbook, and integration with KMS/HSM.
- Q: How is data protected in Hosted mode?
  - A: Hosted data is encrypted in transit and at rest, access is logged in audit trails, and we offer contracts and add-ons for data handling requirements.
- Q: Do you support customer-managed keys (CMK) and HSMs?
  - A: Yes - both for Dedicated/Private. For Hosted customers we offer CMK integrations for enterprise tiers.
- Q: What compliance evidence can you share?
  - A: We maintain SOC2-type evidence and ISO readiness; for enterprise prospects we share a security evidence package under NDA and coordinate with our security team for deeper reviews.
- Q: How do you handle model/data leakage concerns?
  - A: We support model pinning, private model catalogs, and can configure isolation so customer inputs are never used to train public models. We can document retention and purge policies per contract.

10) Demo & discovery playbook (recommended flow - 20-30 min)
  1. 5 min: Intros & candidate persona mapping (who owns latency/cost/SRE/ML infra).
  2. 7-10 min: Prod problem framing + short pitch + Console walkthrough (latency/cost reports, route dashboards).
  3. 5-8 min: Live inference demo using prospect-relevant prompts and showing fallbacks (hosted -> dedicated) and model switching.
  4. 3-5 min: Next steps: pilot offer, data/architecture questionnaire, SOW timeline.

11) Sales assets & owners
- Sales deck (editable): /assets/decks/redwood-inference-sales-deck-2026.pptx - owner: Solutions Engineering (se-ops@redwood.ai).
- TCO calculator (spreadsheet): /assets/tools/tco-calculator-2026.xlsx - owner: RevOps (revops@redwood.ai).
- Security evidence package (NDA required): request via sec-eng@redwood.ai - owner: Security & Compliance.

12) Recommended next steps for AEs
- Use the TCO calc during discovery for high-volume prospects.
- Offer a 4-8 week pilot: hosted eval -> Dedicated sizing -> Private deployment for enterprise.
- Loop in Solutions Engineering early for architecture review if the prospect mentions on-prem, HSM, or strict audit needs.

Appendix: Useful snippets & commands for demos
- Quick curl example (Hosted):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" -d '{"model":"redwood-v1","input":"Summarize the following support ticket..."}'

- Example AJAX snippet (SDK):
  const response = await RedwoodClient.generate({ model: 'redwood-v1', input: prompt });

End of document. For any specific prospect requests (pricing anchors, compliance docs), open a ticket with RevOps or Security and attach the prospect ID.
